newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn imposed 15 pct spending cuts from May 1 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bonn imposed 15 pct spending cuts from May 1 - paper.

text.p: The German finance ministry has imposed spending cuts on all government departments as of May 1, the German daily Berliner Morgenpost said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said all payments from government departments had been cut by 15 percent with immediate affect from May 1.
The finance ministry was not immediately available for comment.
The newspaper report said the move had been communicated to all top-level government officials via a signed circular from a state secretary in the finance ministry, Manfred Overhaus.
It said those people most effected by the cap would be institutions and organisations financed by the government.

The German government is under pressure to reduce spending and raise revenue as it scrambles to meet the three percent deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) goal for Europe's monetary union, due to start in 1999.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said that a complete freeze on new spending could not be ruled out.

Many independent economists said Germany's 1997 deficit will miss the target, with high unemployment and low revenues taking their toll of state coffers, but the government is sticking by it forecast for a 2.9 percent deficit/GDP ratio.

The May tax estimates for 1997 are due on Thursday, with analysts predicting that a shortfall of as much as 20 billion marks may be announced, Waigel to take what some say must be drastic steps to cut spending.
The government has said it expects a shortfall of around eight billion marks.
